angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,641,852 km at 99.01 pc = 0.22 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.0997 +/- 0.0293 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 99.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 2.36 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract): 1,641,852 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.03 +/- 0.066 solar masses from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 8000 +/- 80 K from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-189.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.000, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
